question.problem:
What is the intersection of the intervals shown below, expressed as a number line?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/e2da9ff989c1cee3365f88b4ba7bc8dba9ef31f20dc49ae8e4f87a79243473b0.png)
question.worked_solution:
The intersection of two intervals consists of the values that are in both intervals. So, it can be graphed by finding where the two intervals overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/4333901508bff833b854769feabb729b836cdb3aae9827b5170546b2ffbe7d35.png)

Therefore, the number line that shows the common set of values is:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/f9d3a9e1da4be61938e41eb5ebe308ed85cd1f60f4fd29f211b2f72071afe159.png)

**Watch out!** The point $-1$ is not included in the intersection since it does not lie in the second interval.
